why: A design-style task: a dict of records, each a dict of field -> (value, expiry). Levels add sorted scans, TTL checks on read, and backups that store remaining TTLs and re-base them on restore.
hints: Model the database as key -> {field: (value, expiresAt or None)}. Every read filters out fields whose expiry has passed.
TTL is a half-open interval [timestamp, timestamp + ttl): a field is alive at time t iff expiresAt is None or t < expiresAt. Scans sort the alive fields by name and format them as field(value).

For backup, deep-copy alive fields as (value, remaining = expiresAt - t). For restore at time t, find the latest backup at or before timestampToRestore (bisect on backup times) and rebuild with expiresAt = t + remaining. Each op is O(fields in the record log fields).
pitfalls: A field that expires exactly at t is already gone at t.
delete on an expired field returns false.
backup counts only non-empty records after dropping expired fields.
A restored record keeps its remaining TTL measured at backup time, not its original TTL.
